storyboard.addedInformation: Names the price of dying rich before the hosts explain it: refused surf trips, sabbaticals, dinners at age nine.
storyboard.claim: The richest corpse won nothing; every dollar left at death is an experience refused while the body still worked.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A cemetery hill at dusk with a headstone; Everyman slumped beside the grave.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Cold open.

storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the hoarding as a physical clutching the narration only describes as an abstract habit.
storyboard.claim: We spend decades hoarding abstract wealth while ignoring what it costs.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman in a suburban living room clutching a wallet, worried, mid-realization.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the grave to the habit that fills it: the hoarding behind the corpse.

storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the expiry date a physical form: the clock on the wall and the hourglass running in hand.
storyboard.claim: Money has a biological expiration date printed on the body.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A clock looming over Everyman, who holds an hourglass in dark chart-space.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names what the hoarder ignores: the deadline on the currency.

storyboard.addedInformation: Stages the programming as a young worker receiving the doctrine at his desk.
storyboard.claim: A whole generation was programmed from the first paycheck to save and never spend.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman seated at a trading-office desk at career start, absorbing the doctrine.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the deadline to who was never told about it: the programmed generation.

storyboard.addedInformation: The strike marks the doctrine as rejected: the coin is clutched, not celebrated.
storyboard.claim: The doctrine says save, compound, delay gratification, die responsibly.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman clutching a coin fearfully in the living room, reciting the saver doctrine he obeys.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Spells out the programming introduced in the previous beat.

storyboard.addedInformation: Stages the sleepwalk literally: a worried man walking a quiet suburban street toward the wrong bankruptcy.
storyboard.claim: Millions sleepwalk into the only bankruptcy that matters: outliving their health, not their money.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman walking a suburban street, worried, sleepwalking into the health bankruptcy.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Stress-tests the doctrine: the saver doctrine leads here.

storyboard.addedInformation: Holds the contradiction in one frame: a full wallet gripped by a failing body.
storyboard.claim: Holding a full bank account past the point the body can spend it is tragedy, not discipline.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman gripping a full wallet, worried, body spent.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Completes the bankruptcy image: full account, spent body.

storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the term as show commentary: the host names the new paradigm in chart-space.
storyboard.claim: Temporal economics replaces the currency lens: evaluate life through time, not dollars.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host holding a coin up against a fading clock: currency weighed against time.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Pivots from the tragedy to the paradigm that explains it.

storyboard.addedInformation: Freezes the abstraction: the coin in hand is literally the traded hours.
storyboard.claim: Dollars, euros and portfolios are frozen lifetime: traded hours made solid.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman surprised, holding a coin that reads as frozen time in chart-space.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Defines the new paradigm's unit: money as stored hours.

storyboard.addedInformation: Adds the body's stamp: the hourglass shows the stored energy draining with the body.
storyboard.claim: Money is stored human energy with an invisible expiry date on the body.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman holding an hourglass draining in chart-space.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Stamps the frozen time with its expiry: the body sets the date.

storyboard.addedInformation: Stages the thaw as a reach: unspent energy evaporates if never grabbed in time.
storyboard.claim: Unthawed life energy evaporates: use it while the machine still runs.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman reaching for the draining energy before it evaporates.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The consequence of the expiry: spend it or watch it vanish.

storyboard.addedInformation: Points at the self: the money was never paper, it was traded days of life.
storyboard.claim: Money is not paper or screen zeros; it is pieces of lifespan traded away.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman pointing at himself in the living room, realizing the trade.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Restates the reframe as identity: your money is your days.

storyboard.addedInformation: Introduces the mentor on screen: the energy trader turned life optimizer, not just a name.
storyboard.claim: Bill Perkins, energy trader and poker player, architected this philosophy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Bill Perkins in a navy blazer in the trading office, presenting himself.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the architect after the philosophy he built.

storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the savant at work: risk-reward calculation turned from markets to mortality.
storyboard.claim: A risk-reward savant motivated not by spreadsheets but by watching his circle.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Perkins weighing risk against reward on a balance: calculation beyond the spreadsheet.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From who he is to how he thinks: the calculating eye turns to friends.

storyboard.addedInformation: Puts the hedge-fund friend on screen: wealthy, intense, seated among his millions at 60-plus.
storyboard.claim: Ultra-rich friends hit their 60s and 70s with tens of millions intact.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Perkins pointing out his wealthy friends: tens of millions intact in their 60s and 70s, the watcher not the owner.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows what Perkins watched: the rich friends aging beside their money.

storyboard.addedInformation: Slumps the winner: the money game won, the life game lost, memory banks empty.
storyboard.claim: They won the money game and lost the life game, dying with starved memory banks.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The wealthy man slumped, sad, amid comfort he never converted to memory.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The verdict on the rich friends: victory in money, defeat in life.

storyboard.addedInformation: Boxes the thesis at the cemetery: the grave is the frame the whole dive argues against.
storyboard.claim: The core thesis is dying with zero: plan the curve, not the pile.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host at the cemetery hill naming the thesis over the grave.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the thesis the tragedy demands: the alternative to the rich corpse.

storyboard.addedInformation: Strikes the misreading: the worried face rejects the Vegas caricature, not the book.
storyboard.claim: Die with zero is not reckless Vegas nihilism; that reading is rejected.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman worried in chart-space, pushing away the reckless caricature.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Clears the aggressive phrase before defining what it really means.

storyboard.addedInformation: Reframes the book as analysis: a clinical audit of life energy, not a spending spree.
storyboard.claim: It is the opposite: an analytical autopsy of wasted life energy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host dissecting the waste clinically in chart-space.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Replaces the struck caricature with the real definition.

storyboard.addedInformation: Aims the viewer: the target is fulfillment points, with net worth demoted to fuel.
storyboard.claim: Optimize for fulfillment points, not net worth points.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman pointing at the target: fulfillment aimed at, net worth beside it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: States the optimization rule the autopsy prescribes.

storyboard.addedInformation: Returns to the grave as method: the autopsy starts at the ending on purpose.
storyboard.claim: Start where the journey ends: autopsy the rich death first.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host at the cemetery, beginning the audit at its endpoint.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the thesis into method: back to the grave, deliberately.

storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the worshipped object: the estate held up like a prize for discipline.
storyboard.claim: Society treats a massive estate at death as the ultimate badge of discipline.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman holding up the estate-coin like a trophy in the living room.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the wiring the autopsy attacks: the praised estate.

storyboard.addedInformation: Mourns the irony: the funeral whispers praise over a $4M Vanguard balance nobody enjoyed.
storyboard.claim: A $4M Vanguard balance at the funeral draws whispers of responsibility.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Mourners whispering admiration over the casket: the four-million saver praised, the irony intact.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Concretizes the badge: the $4M funeral everyone admires.

storyboard.addedInformation: Strikes the pity: the sad slump is the judged zero-balance elder the crowd pities.
storyboard.claim: Hitting zero at 90 draws pity, but Perkins says that pity is misplaced.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An elder Everyman slumped under the crowd's misplaced pity.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Flips the funeral irony: the pitied zero-balance elder.

storyboard.addedInformation: Points at the error: the unspent dollars are exhibit A of the miscalculated equation.
storyboard.claim: Dying with millions is not discipline but a structural miscalculation of life's equation.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Perkins pointing at the unspent coin-evidence in the office.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Perkins overturns both verdicts: millions left is the real failure.

storyboard.addedInformation: Lands the charge personally: every unspent dollar is unpaid labor, from the mentor's mouth.
storyboard.claim: Every unspent dollar is life worked for free, and this is not a rogue edgy theory.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Perkins leveling the charge, face grave: years of labor banked for nothing.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Prices the miscalculation: the dollars cost unpaid life.

storyboard.addedInformation: Adds the heavyweight backing: a Nobel-winning hypothesis behind the poker player's claim.
storyboard.claim: Serious economics backs this: Modigliani's life-cycle hypothesis won the Nobel.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host presenting the prize-winning theory in chart-space.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Armors the charge with authority: economics agrees.

storyboard.addedInformation: Diagrams the rational life: wealth spread deliberately so the curve lands on zero at death.
storyboard.claim: A perfectly rational person spreads wealth to reach exactly zero at death.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A cause-effect flow in chart-space: spread wealth across life toward zero at death, Everyman thinking it through.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Formalizes the Nobel rule as the video's structural diagram.

storyboard.addedInformation: Internalizes the economics: money's worth is only what it converts into.
storyboard.claim: Money's only intrinsic value is utility: what it converts into.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman aiming at a zero-date target: utility, not pile.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Defines money's worth after the zero-target rule: conversion, not pile.

storyboard.addedInformation: Slumps under the math: the surplus is proof of utility never claimed.
storyboard.claim: Dying with surplus mathematically fails to maximize the utility of limited Earth time.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman slumped worried beside the unmaximized surplus.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Scores the surplus: the math of the failure.

storyboard.addedInformation: weak: transitional banter beat, staging only; the visceral scene it cues carries the meaning.
storyboard.claim: The hosts pivot to making the math visceral for the listener.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host bridging from theory to the cubicle scene.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Breathes between the theorem and its visceral staging.

storyboard.addedInformation: Seats the viewer in the cubicle: fluorescent hum, late Tuesday, the traded evening made visible.
storyboard.claim: Picture the gray cubicle at 7:15 PM on a Tuesday under buzzing fluorescents.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman seated sad in the gray cubicle at night under fluorescent light.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the visceral scene: the traded evening itself.

storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the spreadsheet as notes in hand: throbbing back, arbitrary goal, future self as payee.
storyboard.claim: A throbbing back over a spreadsheet, chasing a savings goal for a future self.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman seated with spreadsheet notes, aching, chasing the arbitrary goal.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Zooms into the cubicle: the spreadsheet and the sore back.

storyboard.addedInformation: Ages the saver in place: the vibrant Tuesday traded to a self too tired or sick to spend it.
storyboard.claim: That future self may be too tired or sick to spend what youth traded away.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman worried at the desk, facing the frail future self who inherits the number.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Reveals the payee: a future self who cannot spend it.

storyboard.addedInformation: Slumps at the screen: the digital number stays a number, the warning confirmed.
storyboard.claim: A digital number never converted into anything: exactly what Modigliani warned.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman slumped before the glowing unconverted number on screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Closes the cubicle scene: the number that never became life.

storyboard.addedInformation: Visualizes the black hole: worked hours and family time vanishing into unspent money.
storyboard.claim: Every hour worked for unspent money is life energy thrown into a black hole.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman slumped in dark space as life energy drains into a black hole.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Generalizes the cubicle: every unspent hour is the same hole.

storyboard.addedInformation: Clutches the tickets: food processed, effort spent, family time traded for a medium never used.
storyboard.claim: You hoarded the tickets but never went to the carnival.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman sad in the living room clutching the wallet of unused tickets.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Punchlines the waste: tickets hoarded, carnival missed.

storyboard.addedInformation: Bridges to the case study: the host's gut-punch cues Elizabeth's story.
storyboard.claim: A concrete case from the book punches the hosts in the gut.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The surprised host introducing the case that proves the carnival line.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Tees up the proof: from metaphor to a real life.

storyboard.addedInformation: Introduces the foil on her street: the neat, ordinary, perfectly responsible American saver.
storyboard.claim: Elizabeth is the perfectly responsible American: median income, lifelong saver.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Elizabeth, neat in cardigan and glasses, on her quiet suburban street.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Meets the case study: responsibility personified.

storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the lifetime balance: decades of median-income work converted to home equity and savings at 65.
storyboard.claim: She works her whole life on median income and retires at 65 with full net worth.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Elizabeth seated with her lifetime wallet: home equity and savings at retirement.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Builds Elizabeth's ledger before the next chunk reveals its tragic remainder.
